title: Soergel Intersection Forms and Hodge Theory

items.title: The real type-A Soergel category by scalar extension
items.statement: Extend Q→R and set S=R[x_1,...,x_n] with deg x_i=2, with the place-permuting S_n action. The Hodge page uses the coordinate/length normalization of the published reflection realization: alpha_i here means beta_i=x_i-x_{i+1}, and alpha_i^vee means beta_i^vee, so adjacent Cartan entries are -1. The published alternating balanced roots eps_i beta_i are used for diagrammatic presentations, not for positivity on this page. Both choices have identical reflections, invariant rings and underlying bimodules. Define B_i^R=S⊗_{S^{s_i}}S(1) and the real Soergel category as the idempotent completion of their finite additive graded tensor closure, with the same shifts as the rational category. Its unit is the graded ring S (as an object in cohomological degree zero), not a polynomial ring concentrated in internal degree zero. For a rational bimodule M write M^R=M⊗_Q R; the generator and Bott-Samelson constructions extend in this way. Standard graph supports, Delta/nabla flags and characters use the formulas of the rational page over R; the Hecke algebra remains the same integral normalized algebra. The dominant chamber is Theta={rho=Σ c_j x_j: c_i>c_{i+1} for all i}. It is nonempty, for example c_j=(n+1)/2-j.
items.strategy: The place permutation action and coordinate roots/coroots are explicitly supplied by the published two-normalization realization. We fix the coordinate choice for every alpha, Demazure trace and positivity condition on this Hodge page. The invariant-ring tensor bimodules do not change when a root is multiplied by -1; only the chosen Demazure/trace normalization changes, so no diagrammatic presentation is silently reinterpreted. The polynomial ring has S_0=R and finite-dimensional homogeneous pieces. Flat extension of Q to R commutes with the finite free presentations, invariant decomposition S=S^{s_i}⊕alpha_i S^{s_i}, shifts and tensor products. The idempotent closure is the defined real category; preservation of rational indecomposable labels is proved separately in the comparison lemma. For rho=Σ c_jx_j, rho(alpha_i^vee)=c_i-c_{i+1}; the displayed decreasing coefficients give value 1 at every simple coroot. These are the positive roots x_a-x_b for a<b used by inversion length, with adjacent Cartan entries -1. No alternating-sign dominant chamber or unverified replacement of rho is used.

items.title: The Hecke trace form, its values on the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, and the standard pairing
items.statement: Let H = H_v(n) be the normalized type-A Hecke algebra over A = Z[v^{\pm1}] and let a be the A-linear anti-involution with a(v) = v, a(H_x) = H_{x^{-1}} (the reversal anti-involution of the Hecke page). Define the trace eps: H -> A by eps(H_w) = delta_{e,w} on the standard basis, and the bilinear form (-,-): H x H -> A by (h,h') := eps(a(h)h'). Then: (1) eps and (-,-) are well defined (the H_w are an A-basis); (2) (ph, qh') = pq(h,h') for p,q in A; (3) (hH_s, h') = (h, h'H_s) and (H_sh, h') = (h, H_sh') for all h,h' and all simple reflections s; (4) the standard basis is orthonormal, (H_x,H_y) = delta_{xy}; (5) on the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, (H_x,H_y) in vZ[v] for x != y and (H_x,H_x) in 1 + vZ[v]; (6) the same form is the standard pairing <H_x,H_y> = delta_{xy} used in the type-A Soergel Hom formula, transported through the identification of the normalized standard bases. All statements are integral and use no choice.
items.strategy: First give the normalized standard basis its A-bilinear dot product. On each pair {H_w,H_ws} with ell(ws)=ell(w)+1, right multiplication by H_s has matrix [[0,1],[1,v^{-1}-v]], symmetric for this product; the same holds for left multiplication on {H_w,H_sw}. Thus both generator actions are self-adjoint. Repeated adjunction of the factors of a reduced H_x gives (H_x,H_y)_dot=(1,a(H_x)H_y)_dot=eps(a(H_x)H_y). This proves standard orthonormality and identifies the trace-defined form with the dot product, including bilinearity and the generator-adjunction identities. If underline H_x=Σ_u h_{u,x}H_u and underline H_y=Σ_u h_{u,y}H_u, the form is Σ_u h_{u,x}h_{u,y}: there is no coefficient conjugation, since the form and reversal anti-involution are A-linear. Each diagonal coefficient h_{x,x}=1, every off-top coefficient is in vZ[v], and unavailable coefficients are zero. Thus when x≠y every product has at least one factor divisible by v; for x=y the unique constant term is 1. This proves the KL trace properties without any positivity theorem. The same orthonormal standard pairing is the published Hom-formula pairing in the normalized Hecke dictionary.

items.title: The reduced Soergel module and the dominant Lefschetz operator
items.statement: Work over S as in the real scalar-extension definition and let k := S/S_+ = R be the residue field of the right action, with quotient map S -> R. For a graded (S,S)-bimodule M which is finite free as a right S-module put Mbar := M \otimes_S R = M/(M S_+), a finite dimensional graded R-vector space; dimensions are written dim_R(Mbar)^i and the graded dimension is dim(Mbar) = sum_i dim_R(Mbar)^i v^{-i}. For a morphism f: M -> M' of bimodules write fbar for its reduction, so that fbar is R-linear. Fix rho \in S_2 with rho(alpha_i^\vee) > 0 for every i (a strictly dominant degree-two element, which exists by the scalar-extension definition) and denote by rho.(-) the left multiplication operator; since M S_+ is stable under left multiplication, rho.(-) descends to a degree-two R-linear endomorphism of Mbar, called the dominant Lefschetz operator on Mbar. For x in S_n and s in S_n a simple reflection the same construction applies to B_x^R B_s^R = (B_x B_s)^R, and the operator L_0 := rho.(-) on the reduced tensor product is the case zeta = 0 of the deformed operator defined later. Also record the descent-detection property: (w rho)(alpha_s^\vee) > 0 if and only if s w > w, for every w in S_n and simple s (so this formula detects left descents; its instance w=x^{-1} detects right descents of x).
items.strategy: For a finite right-free bimodule M, reduction is M/(M S_+) and has finite graded dimension equal to its right rank. Left multiplication preserves this submodule and descends. In the coordinate normalization rho=Σ c_jx_j with c_1>...>c_n, (w rho)(alpha_i^vee)=c_{w^{-1}(i)}-c_{w^{-1}(i+1)}, positive exactly when w^{-1}(i)<w^{-1}(i+1), equivalently ell(s_iw)>ell(w). This elementary inversion criterion proves the stated sign identity directly, and with w=x^{-1} gives the positive coefficient (x^{-1}rho)(alpha_s^vee) when xs>x. The alternating balanced coroots of the diagrammatic presentation are not used in this criterion.

items.title: Indecomposable labels, characters and filtration ranks agree after real scalar extension
items.statement: Let B_w be the rational indecomposable type-A Soergel bimodule and let B_w^R be its real scalar extension. (1) B_w^R is indecomposable; its finite-dimensional degree-zero endomorphism algebra is local with residue field R. If S(w) holds, its degree-zero endomorphism algebra is R, but no rank-one assertion for the full graded endomorphism module is made. (2) Real extension preserves the labels and shifts of all finite Krull-Schmidt decompositions of rational Soergel bimodules, and every real indecomposable is a unique B_w^R(d). (3) Delta/nabla support-filtration multiplicities, characters, reduction by positive-degree right polynomials, and Hom spaces commute with scalar extension; thus character identities over R descend to Q. (4) If xs>x and S(y) holds for all y<xs, then B_xB_s = B_xs ⊕ ⊕_{y<xs} B_y^{a_y} with a_y nonnegative integers and no grading shifts; the top summand occurs once. If xs<x and S(x) holds, then B_xB_s = B_x(1) ⊕ B_x(-1). All assertions concern the normalized self-dual indecomposables.
items.strategy: First justify base change of Hom by viewing it in a fixed degree as the kernel of the finitely many Q-linear equations expressing compatibility with the left and right polynomial generators. Finite graded right-free presentations and flatness of Q→R commute with these kernels. Support cuts are kernels of annihilator-ideal multiplication maps; the finite support flags split as right modules, so scalar extension also commutes with their quotients, ranks and reduction. For absolute indecomposability put A=End^0_Q(B_w), finite dimensional and local by the published Krull-Schmidt classification. Restrict endomorphisms to the unique rank-one top-support layer: this is a unital algebra map A→Q, surjective because scalar identities restrict to all scalars. Its kernel is the unique maximal ideal J of A; it is nilpotent. To justify nilpotence locally, the descending chain J^k stabilizes in finite dimension and the elementary Nakayama argument applied to its stable term forces that term to be zero: a minimal finite A-generating set for a nonzero stable term cannot exist, since expressing its last generator as a J-linear combination of those generators and inverting 1 minus its last coefficient eliminates that generator. Hence A⊗R has nilpotent ideal J⊗R with quotient R; every element outside that ideal is invertible by a finite geometric series after choosing its scalar lift. Thus A⊗R is local and B_w^R is indecomposable. Decomposing rational Bott-Samelson sums and applying finite Krull-Schmidt uniqueness over R proves the real classification and label comparison. Under S(w), the Hom formula and the constant-term property of the KL trace pairing give End^0(B_w^R)=R; the graded rank is (H_w,H_w), generally not 1. For (4), top support gives B_xs once and only shifted B_y with y<xs otherwise. Since ch(B_xB_s)=H_x H_s=H_xs+Σ μ_y H_y, the Hom formula and the trace-pairing lemma give Hom^j(B_y,B_xB_s)=0 for j<0 whenever y<xs. A summand B_y(d) would give a nonzero map B_y→B_xB_s(-d), forcing d≤0. Self-duality gives the paired shift -d, forcing d≥0. Thus d=0. For a descent, ch(B_xB_s)=(v+v^{-1})H_x=(v+v^{-1})ch(B_x); injectivity of the character on the split Grothendieck group and Krull-Schmidt uniqueness give the displayed two shifts.

items.title: The trace, the invariant intersection form on Bott-Samelson bimodules and its reduction
items.statement: For a finite word x = s_1...s_m let BS(x) = B_{s_1}...B_{s_m} be the real Bott-Samelson bimodule, with its right (and left) S-basis of subexpression elements c_epsil on and the top element c_top := c_{s_1}...c_{s_m}; recall BS(x)(-m) is a commutative ring under termwise multiplication. Define the trace Tr: BS(x) -> S to be the coefficient of c_top when an element is written in the basis {c_epsil on} as a right S-module, and define the intersection form by <b,b'> := Tr(b b'), the product taken in the commutative ring BS(x)(-m). Then: (1) <,> is a graded symmetric form, S-bilinear for the right action, invariant in the sense <rb,b'> = <b,rb'> and <br,b'> = <b,b'r>; (2) if B is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of shifts of Bott-Samelson bimodules, then an invariant form on B is obtained by restriction and is unique up to the choices of the ambient forms; (3) for a self-dual bimodule B the induced form on BB_s is characterised by the three formulas for alpha(b) = b c_id and beta(b) = b c_s: <alpha b, alpha b'> = partial_s(<b,b'>), <alpha b, beta b'> = <b,b'> = <beta b, alpha b'>, <beta b, beta b'> = <b,b'> alpha_s; (4) the intersection form on a Bott-Samelson bimodule is non-degenerate as an S-valued form, and for any summand B of a Bott-Samelson bimodule the restricted form is non-degenerate whenever the summand has finite free right S-rank and the corresponding reduced form is non-degenerate (graded Nakayama); (5) the reduction to Mbar is a graded symmetric R-valued form <,>bar, and non-degeneracy of the S-valued form is equivalent to graded non-degeneracy of the R-valued form; (6) Bott-Samelson bimodules and the indecomposable B_w^R are self-dual, so dim(B_w^R bar)^{-i} = dim(B_w^R bar)^{i} for all i (symmetric Betti numbers). Additionally record the left/right asymmetry: the form is bilinear for the right action and satisfies <rb,b'> = <b,rb'>.
items.strategy: Items (1),(3) are direct computations in the commutative ring BS(x)(-m) and the multiplication rules c_id c_id = c_id, c_id c_s = c_s, c_s c_s = c_s alpha_s, using the identity Tr(chi_i gamma) = Tr_i(gamma); (2) is the induced-form calculation with the basis {alpha(e_i), beta(e_i)} and its dual; (4) is the determinant computation with the block matrix having identity diagonal blocks and the vanishing lower-left block (partial_s(1) = 0); (5) is the graded Nakayama lemma applied to the free right S-module together with the observation that an invariant form is the same as a bimodule map B -> DB. For (6), self-duality of Bott-Samelson bimodules follows from the explicit dual basis of the commutative presentation, and self-duality of B_w^R is a consequence of the base-change classification lemma proved on this page (the rational statement is part of the published type-A classification, and self-duality is preserved by the flat base change Q -> R).

items.title: Primitive subspaces, hard Lefschetz and the Hodge-Riemann signs: the dictionary of hypotheses S, hL and HR
items.statement: Let H be a finite-dimensional graded real space with a graded nondegenerate symmetric form, and let L have degree two and be symmetric for the form. Hard Lefschetz (hL) means L^i:H^{-i}→H^i is an isomorphism for every i≥0. Define P_L^{-i}=ker(L^{i+1}|_{H^{-i}}) for i≥0 and the Lefschetz form (a,b)_L^{-i}=<a,L^i b>. Under hL the primitive decomposition is H=⊕_{i≥0}⊕_{j=0}^i L^j P_L^{-i}, proved in the primitive-decomposition lemma. Assume H is concentrated in one parity and its lowest nonzero degree is -d. HR with standard sign means hL and (-1)^{(d-i)/2}-definiteness on P_L^{-i} for every i≥0; the bottom primitive form is positive. A sign with odd exponent numerator means the primitive space is zero. HR with either global sign allows a common factor epsilon∈{±1}. For B_xbar use d=ell(x), L=left rho. S(x) means ch(B_x)=underline H_x. Under S(x), HR(x) uses the positively normalized intrinsic invariant form; HRbar(x) requires HR for every reduced-word summand embedding, and the invariant-form lemma proves their equivalence. The strong embedded-form HRbar(x) makes sense without S(x). For xs>x the analogous package on B_xB_s has bottom degree -ell(x)-1 and primitive sign (-1)^{(ell(x)+1-i)/2}; HR(x,s) refers to a fixed reduced-word induced form and HRbar(x,s) to all such choices. Their deformed versions use L_zeta from its Definition. S^±(y,x,s) uses the local-intersection-form Definition. For an orthogonal L-stable direct sum, HR is equivalent to HR on the summands with the same ambient degree-dependent signs, which need not be each summand's own standard sign if their bottom degrees differ.
items.strategy: This fixes the centered grading and standard-sign normalization. The sign on primitives in degree -i is (-1)^{(d-i)/2}; it is positive at i=d and alternates every two degrees upward. For an indecomposable of length ell it equals (-1)^{(ell-i)/2}=(-1)^{(i-ell)/2}, precisely EW Theorem 1.4. For the tensor product in an ascent replace ell by ell(x)+1. The parity-only formula epsilon(-1)^{(-i+j)/2}, j=0 or 1, is equivalent after choosing epsilon to make the bottom form positive, and is not imposed simultaneously without that factor. Substantive primitive decomposition and form-normalization equivalences are proved by the named local lemmas. Orthogonal blocks use the common ambient signs; the tensoring lemma computes the necessary scalar signs explicitly.

items.title: Minimal complexes and the perverse truncations in the real type-A Soergel category
items.statement: Let B be the real graded type-A Soergel category with degree-zero morphisms. Its categorical radical consists of f:M→N for which 1_M-gf is invertible for every g:N→M; write q:B→B^ss=B/rad B. A bounded complex is minimal when all differentials become zero after q. A Soergel bimodule is perverse when its character is a nonnegative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis elements (not the standard basis); it is p-split when its indecomposable summands are shifts of perverse ones. For a p-split decomposition M=⊕ B_x(k)^{m_{x,k}}, with the normalized B_x perverse, set tau_{≤j}M=⊕_{k≥-j}B_x(k)^{m_{x,k}}, tau_{<j}=tau_{≤j-1}, tau_{≥j}=M/tau_{<j}, and H^j(M)=(tau_{≤j}M/tau_{<j}M)(j). Define pK^b_{≥0} (respectively pK^b_{≤0}) by complexes isomorphic in the homotopy category to complexes whose terms are p-split and satisfy tau_{<-i}(^iF)=0 (respectively ^iF=tau_{≤-i}(^iF)) in each cohomological degree i. Thus their indecomposable shifts k obey k≤i (respectively k≥i). Internal shift (1) changes module degrees; homological shift [1] changes complex degrees. The structural lemma supplies semisimplicity, minimal-model existence/uniqueness, the functoriality of these cuts, and triangle closure.
items.strategy: Define the radical by the invertibility criterion and the minimal/perverse objects by the displayed conditions. The structural lemma proves their claimed well-definedness and model-independent properties; do not assert radical zero for a normalized indecomposable before S(x).

items.title: The Lefschetz operator factors through deleted Bott-Samelson subwords, with positive rescalings
items.statement: Let x = s_1...s_m be an expression, BS(x) its Bott-Samelson bimodule, Br_i = chi_i o phi_i the Demazure operation at the i-th letter, and Tr, <,> the trace and intersection form. (1) As endomorphisms of BS(x) one has rho.(-) = \Sigma_{i=1}^m (s_{i-1}...s_1 rho)(alpha_{s_i}^\vee) chi_i phi_i + (-).x^{-1}rho (Lemma 3.4). (2) With the rescaled forms <,>'_i := (s_{i-1}...s_1rho)(alpha_{s_i}^\vee) <,>_i on BS(x-hat-i) and <,>' the direct sum, one has <b,rho b'>_{overline{BS(x)}} = <phi(b),phi(b')>' for all b,b' in the reduced module overline{BS(x)}, where phi = \Sigma_i phi_i: BS(x) -> \bigoplus_i BS(x-hat-i)(1) (Lemmas 6.14 and 6.15). (3) If x is reduced then every scaling factor gamma_i := (s_{i-1}...s_1 rho)(alpha_{s_i}^\vee) is strictly positive, so the rescalings change no signs in the HR statements; the un-scattered term (-).x^{-1}rho vanishes after reduction to the Soergel module. (4) Consequently left multiplication by rho on overline{BS(x)} factors, up to positive rescalings, as the composite BS(x) -> \bigoplus_i BS(x-hat-i)(1) -> BS(x)(2), and this composite is the first differential of the Rouquier complex F_{s_1}...F_{s_m} followed by its dual map, up to the same positive rescalings.
items.strategy: (1) is the explicit computation with the multiplication rule r.c_id = c_id.(sr) + partial_s(r)c_s and summation over the letters. (2) is asserted after right reduction, where the right-multiplication remainder vanishes; it follows from the identity Tr(chi_i(gamma)) = Tr_i(gamma) and the definition of phi_i: <b,Br_i b'> = <phi_i b, phi_i b'>_i. (3) uses the strict dominance of rho and the descent-detection property (w rho)(alpha_s^\vee) > 0 iff sw > w applied to the prefixes of the reduced expression. (4) compare with the definition of the generator complexes F_i = [B_i -> R(1)] and the Rouquier complex as the total tensor product: the first differential of F_{s_1}...F_{s_m} is the sum of the maps phi_i at the deleted subwords, and the composite with the rescaled dual maps is left multiplication by rho on the reduced Bott-Samelson module. Verify the sign conventions of the shift in the published Rouquier page before writing the identification.

items.title: Invariant forms on an indecomposable Soergel bimodule are unique up to scalar, non-degenerate, and agree with the restricted Bott-Samelson form
items.statement: Assume S(x), i.e. ch(B_x^R) = H_x. Then: (1) the space of invariant forms on B_x^R is one dimensional over R, and every non-zero invariant form is non-degenerate; (2) if B_x^R is embedded as a direct summand of a Bott-Samelson bimodule BS(x) for a reduced expression of x, the restriction of the intersection form is a positive multiple of the intersection form on B_x^R; (3) consequently HR(x) holds for the intrinsic intersection form if and only if HRbar(x) holds for every (equivalently: some) embedding, and the two normalizations differ by a positive scalar, so no sign changes; (4) if B = \oplus_z B_z^{R,m_z} with S(z) for all z, then nondegenerate symmetric invariant forms on B are direct sums of the forms on the isotypic components tensored with nonsingular real symmetric multiplicity-space pairings, and an orthogonal decomposition into isotypic components can always be chosen.
items.strategy: Under S(x), the degree-zero Hom formula gives dim_R Hom^0(B_x,D B_x)=dim_R End^0(B_x)=1; this is not a rank-one assertion about Hom^bullet. Self-duality supplies an isomorphism B_x→D B_x, so each nonzero degree-zero invariant form is a nonzero real scalar multiple of a nondegenerate one. For a reduced-word embedding B_x→BS(x), the bottom degree is one-dimensional and maps isomorphically to the Bott-Samelson bottom degree. Its Lefschetz value is positive: expand rho^{ell(x)} on the bottom subexpression using the deleted-letter identity and induct on the length. Every reduced deletion has a positive coefficient (s_{i-1}...s_1rho)(alpha_{s_i}^vee) and positive top value by induction; nonreduced deletions contribute zero by degree bounds. Hence the restricted form is nonzero and its scalar comparison with the normalized intrinsic form is positive. This proves (1)-(3). For (4), S(z) and S(y) give Hom^0(B_z,D B_y)=0 for z≠y, so the isotypic components are orthogonal. On each component the invariant form is a real symmetric matrix on the multiplicity space tensored with the normalized form on B_z; if the total form is nondegenerate this matrix is nonsingular. Diagonalizing it gives an orthogonal sum of scalar copies. Definiteness of its sign is an additional HR input in the tensoring lemma, not an automatic consequence of nondegeneracy.

items.title: Hard Lefschetz gives the primitive decomposition, orthogonality and the signature formula
items.statement: Let H have a graded nondegenerate symmetric form and a symmetric degree-two operator L. If hL holds then H=⊕_{i≥0}⊕_{j=0}^i L^jP_L^{-i}. In each degree -i≥-d, the decomposition H^{-i}=⊕_{k≥0}L^kP_L^{-(i+2k)} is orthogonal for the Lefschetz form <a,L^i b>. All Lefschetz forms on H^{-i} are nondegenerate exactly when hL holds. If H has one parity and lowest degree -d, standard HR is equivalent to hL and, for every i≥0, sig(<-,L^i ->|_{H^{-i}})=Σ_{k≥0}(-1)^{(d-i-2k)/2}dim P_L^{-(i+2k)} (zero spaces omitted). An L-stable graded subspace V with symmetric dimensions inherits hL; if H satisfies HR, its restricted form is nondegenerate and it inherits the ambient primitive signs. Its standard global sign agrees with that of H when their lowest degrees coincide.
items.strategy: Under hL, L^{i+2}:H^{-i-2}→H^{i+2} is invertible. For a∈H^{-i}, solve L^{i+2}b=L^{i+1}a and write a=(a-Lb)+Lb with the first term primitive. The intersection is zero by the same invertibility. Thus H^{-i}=P^{-i}⊕L H^{-i-2}; iteration and hL give the full primitive strings and dim P^{-i}=dim H^{-i}-dim H^{-i-2}. Symmetry of L makes this decomposition orthogonal: <p,L^{i+1}b>=<L^{i+1}p,b>=0. More generally the Lefschetz form on L^kP^{-(i+2k)} identifies with the primitive form <p,L^{i+2k}q>. Nondegeneracy of the original pairing identifies invertibility of L^i with nondegeneracy of its Lefschetz form. Taking signatures of those orthogonal pieces gives the displayed sum. Conversely descend from the bottom degree: subtract the already-determined lower primitive-string signatures to obtain the signature of each new primitive form. It equals plus or minus its full dimension; together with nondegeneracy this gives definiteness and the HR signs. For V, L^i is injective by inherited hL and is surjective by dimension symmetry. Apply the same primitive-decomposition construction inside V; its primitive spaces are V∩P_H^{-i} and the definite primitive forms restrict to them. Orthogonal primitive strings then give restricted nondegeneracy and ambient signs. This proves the stable-subspace assertion without assuming its primitive projectors preserve an arbitrary subspace in advance.

items.title: The deformed Lefschetz operator L_zeta on B_x B_s
items.statement: Fix x in S_n, a simple reflection s and a strictly dominant rho. For zeta≥0 define L_zeta=(rho·(-))⊗id_{B_s}+id_{B_x}⊗(zeta rho·(-)) on B_xB_s. The second term is multiplication at the middle tensor position, equivalently right rho multiplication on B_x, and is well-defined on the balanced tensor product. These commuting degree-two operators descend to the reduced module and are symmetric for the induced invariant form. Write hL(x,s)_zeta, HR(x,s)_zeta and HRbar(x,s)_zeta for the centered hard Lefschetz, Hodge-Riemann and strong embedded-form statements with this operator. L_0 is left multiplication by rho, so the zero-parameter statements equal hL(x,s), HR(x,s), HRbar(x,s). The family is polynomial in zeta. A bimodule summand is automatically stable under L_0; stability under a middle-position operator must be checked separately. The undeformed summand implications used in the induction are supplied by the local restriction lemma, after deforming back to zeta=0.
items.strategy: Check balancing: for b r⊗c=b⊗r c, both compositions with middle rho give b r⊗rho c=b⊗rho r c since the polynomial ring is commutative. All terms are right-linear, so preserve the right augmentation ideal. Invariance of the form proves symmetry separately for left multiplication on the first tensor factor and left multiplication on the second factor. The identities at zero and polynomial dependence are direct calculations. Do not infer hL(xs) or HR(xs) by restricting L_zeta to a chosen bimodule summand at positive zeta; use the separately proved undeformed restriction lemma.

items.title: Radical quotients, minimal complexes and perverse filtrations in the Soergel category
items.statement: The radical quotient B^ss is semisimple with simple classes B_x(k) and their endomorphism rings R; q reflects isomorphisms. Every bounded complex has a minimal direct summand whose inclusion is a homotopy equivalence, and any two minimal models are isomorphic as complexes. Every direct summand of a perverse (respectively p-split) bimodule is perverse (respectively p-split). For perverse M,N, Hom(M,N(-i))=0 for i>0. The perverse cuts on p-split bimodules are independent of their decompositions and preserved by every morphism. The definitions of pK^b_{≥0} and pK^b_{≤0} can equivalently be tested on the minimal model, and both classes are closed under extensions in distinguished triangles.
items.strategy: Finite Krull-Schmidt decomposition and the base-change lemma give local finite-dimensional End^0(B_x(k)) with residue R. For a finite sum, quotient by its categorical radical is the product of matrix algebras over these residue fields, grouped by identical (x,k); all cross-class maps vanish there. The radical is nilpotent by the same finite-dimensional minimal-generator argument as in the base-change lemma. If q(f) is invertible, lift a two-sided inverse; the errors in the two compositions lie in these nilpotent radicals, so the finite geometric-series inverse proves f invertible. To minimize a bounded complex, if a differential survives q, isolate a nonzero matrix entry between identical simple classes, lift it to an invertible block, and apply Gaussian elimination. Each cancellation removes two indecomposable terms, so finitely many cancellations suffice. Between minimal models a homotopy equivalence becomes an ordinary degreewise isomorphism after q, since q-differentials are zero; isomorphism reflection gives an isomorphism of complexes. For perversity, a summand character has nonnegative standard-basis coefficients and is bar invariant. Since the total perverse character has no negative powers in that basis, each summand also has no negative powers. Its KL expansion, obtained by triangular subtraction, has coefficients in Z[v]; bar invariance forces each coefficient to be constant, and its constant equals the nonnegative constant of the standard coefficient, since the lower terms of each KL basis element are divisible by v. Thus summands are perverse. The p-split claim follows by indecomposable decomposition. The Hom formula on two constant KL expansions has no negative degrees, giving the asserted negative-shift vanishing. For shifted perverse objects, a map B_x(k)→B_y(l) can only exist if l-k≥0. Thus maps preserve the subobject defined by k≥-j; applying this to a change of decomposition and its inverse proves intrinsicness and functoriality of the cuts. A minimal model is obtained by removing pairs from a model; the cut bounds persist under direct summands. Finally, for a triangle F'→F→F''→ with F',F'' in either bound, choose representatives satisfying the termwise bounds and represent F by the cone of F''[-1]→F'. Its ith term is ^iF'⊕^iF'', which satisfies the same cut. This proves extension closure and supplies the preliminary properties used by the linearity and HR proofs.

items.title: Positive Rouquier complexes are Delta-split
items.statement: Let x be a reduced expression for x in S_n and let F_x be the Rouquier complex F_{s_1}...F_{s_m} in K^b(SBim_n^R) (or its minimal subcomplex). Then for every y in S_n there is an isomorphism in the homotopy category of graded bimodules Gamma_{>=y/>y}(F_x) = Delta_x if y = x, and 0 otherwise. Equivalently: the Bruhat support subquotient of a positive Rouquier complex is contractible except in the top layer Delta_x = R_x(-\ell(x)); F_x is Delta-split in the sense that each of its support subquotients is a direct sum of standard bimodules, and the top layer is a single Delta_x. No positivity of characters and no assumption S is used; the statement is unconditional for every Coxeter group and every reflection faithful realization.
items.strategy: Prove the nabla statement for inverse complexes E_x first and dualize to the displayed Delta statement for F_x, following LW Proposition 3.7, with all required support commutation justified locally. Choose a Bruhat-compatible enumeration in pairs w_{2j},w_{2j+1}=w_{2j}s by enumerating W/<s> and refining each pair. Only finitely many pairs in the current support enter the induction. Each paired prefix A is s-stable. Its support cut Gamma_A M and the quotient have finite standard flags and hence are free as right polynomial modules (split each flag successively). Tensoring Gamma_A M→M with B_s remains injective. Over the fraction field, tensoring with B_s only sends graph labels w to {w,ws}. Thus the resulting submodule is supported in A and the quotient in its complement, because A is s-stable. The quotient is right-free: its standard flag tensors into rank-one/two graph flags, each right-free. Consequently any A-supported element of that quotient vanishes after fraction-field localization and is zero; this proves Gamma_A(MB_s)=(Gamma_A M)B_s. Exactness of tensoring and quotienting gives the same isomorphism for a two-element paired subquotient and hence for tensoring with E_s. This is the commutativity isomorphism of LW (17), now with a local argument rather than importing Williamson Proposition 6.5. The length-zero/one complexes are checked by the explicit rank-one maps. Write x=zs with ell(z)=ell(x)-1. By induction the paired subquotient over {z,x} of E_z is R_z(ell(z)); tensoring E_s gives the two-term rank-one graph-union complex whose two single-graph subquotients are the identity complex at z and R_x(ell(x)) in degree zero at x. For a different pair {y,ys}, both single-layer complexes of E_z are contractible by induction. Their extension splits after restriction to (R,R^s): the two graph modules have identical invariant-right action r↦y(r), and a standard-free extension is left-free and annihilated by the common graph ideal (after fraction-field localization, then by torsion-freeness). Thus a left-module splitting is invariant-right-linear. Tensoring B_s gives a termwise split short exact sequence of complexes and hence a triangle with contractible outer terms; the paired B_s product is contractible. The triangle E_z(-1)→E_zB_s→E_zE_s and the zero single-layer factors then show both corresponding layers of E_x vanish. The two support cuts commute with passing to the paired quotient, so these cover every layer. Right/left duality converts nabla cuts to Delta cuts and E_x to F_x, giving the stated Delta-split property. Only rank-one graph calculations, finite support flags, tensor exactness and Gaussian cancellation are used; no character conjecture or positivity theorem is assumed.

items.title: Signature constancy in a Lefschetz family, the L-stable subspace lemma and the weak-Lefschetz substitute
items.statement: Let H be a finite dimensional graded real vector space with a graded non-degenerate symmetric form. (1) Family lemma: if L_t, t in [a,b], is a continuous family of symmetric degree-two operators each satisfying hL, and L_{t_0} satisfies HR with the standard sign for one t_0, then every L_t satisfies hL and the same HR signs; in the application the family is L_zeta for zeta>=0, which is polynomial (hence continuous) in zeta. (2) Weak-Lefschetz substitute: let phi: V -> W(1) be a map of graded R[L]-modules with (a) phi injective in degrees <= -1, (b) graded forms <,>_V, <,>_W with <phi(a),phi(b)>_W = <a,Lb>_V, and (c) W satisfies HR with the standard sign; then L^i: V^{-i} -> V^i is injective for all i >= 0, and if dim V^i = dim V^{-i} for all i then L satisfies hL on V. (3) Sign bookkeeping: if in (2) the lowest degree of W is -l and of V is -(l+1), then the Lefschetz form on V^{-(l+1)} is +/- definite with the same sign as on W^{-l}, so if V satisfies HR with the standard sign then V has the standard sign if and only if W does. (4) Degenerate shifted case: if L^i: H^{-d-i} -> H^{-d+i} is an isomorphism for all i >= 0 with d > 0 (so hL fails in the centered sense) and the form is not assumed non-degenerate, then the Lefschetz form (h,h')^{-i}_L = <h,L^i h'> on H^{-i} is identically zero for i >= 0 (Lemma 2.5). (5) Stable-subspace lemma: if (H,L,<,>) satisfies hL and HR and V⊂H is an L-stable graded subspace with dim V^{-i}=dim V^i for all i, then the restricted operator and form satisfy hL and HR on V, with the ambient degree-by-degree signs. The restricted form is nondegenerate; its standard global sign agrees with the ambient standard sign if the lowest nonzero degrees agree.
items.strategy: (1) is the constancy of the signature on the open set of non-degenerate symmetric matrices along a continuous path: the eigenvalues of a continuous family of symmetric matrices depend continuously on the parameter, so the numbers of positive and negative eigenvalues are locally constant, hence constant on the connected interval. (2) elementary: for 0 != a in V^{-i} with i >= 1, phi(a) is non-zero by injectivity in degrees <= -1; if L^i phi(a) = phi(L^i a) != 0 then L^i a != 0; otherwise phi(a) is primitive and <phi(a),phi(a)>^{-i+1}_L = <a, L^i a>_V is non-zero with a definite sign by the HR relations of W. (3) inspect the lowest-degree case of the same computation. (4) use the shifted primitive decomposition H^m = \oplus_j L^j Q^{m-2j} with Q^{-d-i}_L := ker(L^{i+1}) \subset H^{-d-i} and show <L^j x, L^k y> = <x, L^{j+k-m} y> = 0 because the exponent j+k-m is at least the defining exponent of the primitive condition and d > 0. For (5), inherited injectivity of L^i and symmetry of the dimensions prove hL on V. Its primitive subspaces ker L^{i+1}∩V^{-i} lie in those of H and inherit definite Lefschetz forms. The primitive decomposition of V follows from hL. Orthogonality of primitive strings and the definite primitive forms show that the restricted graded form is nondegenerate and give the asserted signs. Equal lowest degrees give the same standard global sign. In (3) do not assume the conclusion in advance: the computation shows that whenever V satisfies HR (with either global sign), its standard-sign normalization is equivalent to that of W.

items.title: The local intersection form on Hom(B_y, B_x B_s)
items.statement: Fix xs>x and y<xs, and assume S(z) for all z<xs. Choose reduced-word embeddings B_y→BS(y) and B_x→BS(x), their positively normalized nondegenerate invariant forms, and the induced form on M=B_xB_s. On the finite-dimensional real space E_y=Hom^0(B_y,M), define (f,g)^{x,s}_y by the scalar endomorphism g* f∈End^0(B_y)=R, where g* is the adjoint. The adjoint identifies Hom^0(B_y,M) with Hom^0(M,B_y). The form is symmetric and changes only by a positive scalar when the chosen normalized forms/embeddings change. Define S^±(y,x,s) to mean (-1)^{(ell(x)+1-ell(y))/2}-definiteness, with the parity convention of the primitive-space definition. The degree-zero Hom dimension and the equivalence of nondegeneracy with actual summand multiplicities are proved in the detection theorem; no statement identifies the full graded Hom rank with a KL coefficient.
items.strategy: The nondegenerate graded invariant forms identify each bimodule with its dual, so adjoints are well-defined degree-zero bimodule maps. Under S(y), End^0(B_y)=R, giving the scalar-valued composition. The adjoint of g* f is f* g, and a scalar endomorphism is self-adjoint, so the form is symmetric. Scaling the M-form by a positive scalar a and the B_y-form by a positive scalar b scales this form by a/b. The invariant-form uniqueness lemma ensures these comparisons are positive for all chosen reduced-word embeddings. The definition uses degree-zero Hom throughout; its quantitative detection properties have a separate proved supplier.

items.title: Tensoring a direct sum of Hodge-Riemann bimodules with B_s preserves the signs
items.statement: Fix zeta >= 0 and a self-dual Soergel bimodule B = \bigoplus_z B_z^{R,m_z} such that m_z != 0 implies S(z) and HR(z,s)_zeta; if zeta = 0 assume in addition that m_z = 0 whenever zs < z. Assume B is even or odd, carries an invariant non-degenerate form and satisfies HR with the standard sign with respect to left multiplication by rho. Then BB_s satisfies HR with the standard sign with respect to L_zeta and the induced form. More precisely, if the lowest degree of B is -d, then the restriction of its form to a B_z summand is (-1)^{(d-ell(z))/2} times a positive multiple of the normalized form on B_z. Tensoring gives the primitive sign (-1)^{(d+1-i)/2} on degree -i of BB_s, whose lowest degree is -d-1.
items.strategy: Under S(z), the degree-zero Hom formula gives Hom^0(B_z,D B_y)=0 for z≠y and End^0(B_z)=R, so the isotypic decomposition is orthogonal and its invariant forms are scalar matrices on the multiplicity spaces. If the lowest degree of B is -d, the bottom space of each B_z summand (degree -ell(z)) is primitive for rho. HR on B says that the induced multiplicity-space Lefschetz form has sign (-1)^{(d-ell(z))/2}. Choose an orthogonal basis in that definite space and use End^0(B_z)=R to obtain orthogonal indecomposable copies; their restricted invariant forms are that sign times positive multiples of the normalized intersection form. The induced tensor-product forms preserve this orthogonal decomposition into B_zB_s blocks, and L_zeta preserves these blocks because the projections on B commute with its left and right actions. On a primitive vector of degree -i, HR(z,s)_zeta gives sign (-1)^{(ell(z)+1-i)/2}; multiplying by the form scalar gives (-1)^{(d+1-i)/2}. This is precisely the common standard HR sign for BB_s. At zero the hypotheses exclude descent summands, so the proof never assumes HR for a shifted descent block; the degenerate-shift analysis is used separately in the zero-parameter hard-Lefschetz theorem.

items.title: Right-descent Soergel bimodules descend to simple invariants under the character hypothesis
items.statement: Let M=B_x over R and let s be a right descent, xs<x. Assume S(x). There is a graded (R,R^s)-bimodule N and an isomorphism M=N⊗_{R^s}R. Consequently M B_s=M(1)⊕M(-1); choosing the decomposition R=R^s⊕(alpha_s/2)R^s in the middle tensor factor, the reduced operator L_zeta has matrix [[rho,0],[zeta rho(alpha_s^vee),rho]], where the scalar off-diagonal entry is a degree-two map from M(1) to M(-1). The construction requires no singular-category classification or character conjecture beyond S(x). If hL(x) also holds and zeta>0 this matrix satisfies centered hard Lefschetz. At zeta=0 it fails centered hard Lefschetz.
items.strategy: The comparison/classification lemma supplies M B_s=M(1)⊕M(-1), End^0(M)=R and the one-dimensional bottom degree M^{-ell(x)}. Write U=M⊗_{R^s}R, so M B_s=U(1). The multiplication counit c:U→M, c(b⊗r)=br, is nonzero on the lowest degree (b⊗1↦b). In U=M⊕M(-2), that lowest degree belongs only to M. Hence the restriction of c to the first summand is a nonzero scalar endomorphism and is invertible. Rescale its inclusion to obtain a graded bimodule section σ:M→U with cσ=id. The twisted counit c_s:U→M_s, c_s(b⊗r)=b s(r), is balanced over R^s and left-linear; its right action is twisted by s. Set t=c_sσ. As a map on the underlying space t is right-s-semilinear, left-linear and degree zero. On the one-dimensional bottom degree σ(b)=b⊗1, so t(b)=b. Therefore t² is an ordinary degree-zero bimodule endomorphism, scalar because End^0(M)=R, with scalar 1 on the bottom degree; hence t²=id. Since s(r)-r is divisible by alpha_s, c_s(u)-c(u) belongs to M alpha_s for every u, and consequently t(m)-m belongs to M alpha_s. Put N={m:t(m)=m}. Every m splits into invariant and anti-invariant parts (m±t(m))/2. An anti-invariant m equals n alpha_s because it is divisible by alpha_s. Right freeness makes alpha_s multiplication injective; t(m)=-m and s(alpha_s)=-alpha_s then imply t(n)=n. Thus M=N⊕N alpha_s as an (R,R^s)-bimodule and multiplication gives N⊗_{R^s}R≅M. This proves the necessary descent seam locally. Compute the operator matrix using inclusion iota_1(r)=r, iota_2(r)=alpha_s r/2 and projections pi_1(r)=(r+s(r))/2, pi_2(r)=∂_s r. They satisfy pi_a iota_b=δ_ab. Multiplication by rho in the middle factor has entries pi_1(rho), pi_1(alpha_s rho)/2, rho(alpha_s^vee), ∂_s(alpha_s rho)/2. All entries except the constant bottom-left entry have positive polynomial degree and become zero as right multiplications on the reduced module. Left rho contributes the same diagonal operator on both shifts. This gives the claimed matrix. Under hL(x), decompose Mbar into centered primitive rho strings. Normalize the nonzero off-diagonal scalar to 1, and on a string u_0,...,u_m of degrees -m,-m+2,...,m let v_-,v_+ have degrees -1,+1. The matrix operator e satisfies e^k(u_j v_-)=u_{j+k}v_-+k u_{j+k-1}v_+ and e^k(u_jv_+)=u_{j+k}v_+, with out-of-range indices zero. In degree -k with 0≤k≤m-1 and k congruent to m+1 modulo 2, a source basis is u_jv_-,u_{j-1}v_+ for j=(m+1-k)/2; the corresponding target basis gives matrix [[1,0],[k,1]], invertible. At the extreme k=m+1 the map sends u_0v_- to (m+1)u_mv_+, nonzero. All other relevant pieces are zero. This proves hL for each two-shift string and hence for their direct sum, without importing sl_2 semisimplicity. At zero the bottom vector of M(1) in degree -ell(x)-1 is killed by rho^{ell(x)+1}, proving failure.

items.title: Minimal positive Rouquier complexes are linear under the lower Soergel induction
items.statement: Assume S(y) for all y <= x (ch(B_y^R) = H_y) and let F_x be a minimal Rouquier complex of a reduced expression of x. Then: (1) ^0F_x = B_x; (2) for every i >= 1, ^iF_x is isomorphic to a direct sum of shifts B_z(i)^{m_{z,i}} with z < x and m_{z,i} in Z_{>=0}; in particular F_x lies in pK^b_{<=0} \cap pK^b_{>=0} and is linear (each summand in homological degree i carries the internal shift exactly i); (3) the multiplicities satisfy the parity vanishing m_{z,i} = 0 unless i and \ell(x)-\ell(z) have the same parity, and consequently, writing the standard basis element H_x = \Sigma_z g_{z,x} underline H_z in the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis (inverse Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients), one has g_{x,x} = 1, g_{z,x} = \Sigma_i(-1)^im_{z,i}v^i, and (-1)^{\ell(x)-\ell(z)}g_{z,x} has non-negative coefficients. Note that the statement is conditional exactly on S(y) for y <= x and does NOT use S(x') for x' > x nor the final Soergel theorem; it is the induction step of the simultaneous induction.
items.strategy: Use Corollary 6.7 (F_x in pK^b_{>=0}, proved by induction on ell(x) from the two lemmas 6.5 and 6.6: for xs < x, B_xF_s = B_x(-1) via the rank-one splitting and contractions; for xs > x, B_xF_s lies in pK^b_{>=0} because the KL multiplication formula and S on the relevant labels give an unshifted lower-summand decomposition and hence perversity in the KL basis) and Lemma 6.11: if ^iF_x contains a summand B_z(j) with z < x, then ^{i-1}F_x contains a summand B_{z'}(j') with z' > z and j' < j. The argument applies Gamma_{>=z/>z} to F_x, uses the Delta-splitness theorem to split the resulting complex, and tracks the summand Delta_z(j): it cannot survive in cohomology, cannot be hit from degree i+1 for degree reasons, and hence is hit from degree i-1, forcing z' > z and j' < j. From Lemma 6.11, ^0F_x has only summands B_x, hence equals B_x (using Gamma_{>=x/>x}); induction gives tau_{>-i}(^iF_x) = 0, i.e. F_x in pK^b_{<=0}. The parity statement is the standard induction on the length filtration: the summands of B_sB_z with sz > z are B_{sz} plus terms B_v with v < z and v of parity opposite to z, so the shift parity propagates as stated. This is the conditional 'linearity' theorem inside the simultaneous induction; no circular appeal to the Soergel theorem is made.

items.title: Undeformed Lefschetz and Hodge-Riemann restrict to the next Soergel summand
items.statement: Let xs>x. The normalized indecomposable B_xs occurs as a bimodule summand of B_xB_s. If hL(x,s)_0 holds, then hL(xs) holds. If S(<xs) and hL(y) for every y<xs hold, then hL(x,s)_0 is equivalent to hL(xs). If HRbar(x,s)_0 holds, then the restriction to the chosen B_xs summand satisfies the Hodge-Riemann relations for its induced form; once S(xs) has been established, positive comparison of invariant forms gives HR(xs) and HRbar(xs) with the standard sign. More generally an L-stable graded subspace with symmetric Betti numbers inherits HR with the ambient signs, and an L-stable graded direct summand inherits hL. These conclusions apply to a positive deformation only if the chosen subspace and, for the direct-sum argument, its complement are preserved by that operator; they make no identification of the restricted positive operator with left rho.
items.strategy: For hL, the inclusion and projection of any bimodule summand commute with left multiplication rho=L_0 and remain split after right reduction. The map L_0^i is block diagonal on the reduced direct sum. If it is invertible, each diagonal block is invertible; in particular its B_xs block is rho^i. Under S(<xs), the comparison/classification lemma gives an unshifted decomposition B_xB_s=B_xs⊕⊕B_y^{a_y}. Hence hL(xs) and hL(y) for lower y make every block invertible, proving the converse. For HR, the reduced B_xs has symmetric Betti numbers by self-duality. Apply the stable-subspace lemma: injectivity of rho^i inherited from the ambient hL plus dimension symmetry gives hL on B_xs; its primitive spaces are intersections with ambient primitive spaces and inherit definite forms. Primitive decomposition proves restricted nondegeneracy. The lowest degrees of B_xs and B_xB_s are both -ell(xs), so the signs and positive normalization agree. For every embedding B_xs→BS(xs), use the multiplicity-one top summand and its positive lowest-degree Lefschetz value to compare restrictions; after S(xs), uniqueness of invariant forms gives a positive scalar comparison with its normalized intersection form. This gives the strong embedded-form formulation and HR(xs). No claim uses stability of an arbitrary bimodule summand under L_zeta for zeta>0.

items.title: Non-degeneracy of the local intersection forms detects Soergel's conjecture one step higher
items.statement: Fix xs>x and assume S(y) for every y<xs. Put M=B_xB_s and write the KL multiplication formula H_x H_s=H_xs+Σ_{y<xs} μ_y H_y, where μ_y are integer constants (zero when absent). For each y<xs, let E_y=Hom^0(B_y,M), and equip E_y with the local intersection form using adjoints of the nondegenerate invariant forms. Then dim_R E_y=μ_y, while the full graded Hom module has graded rank (H_y,H_x H_s), generally not μ_y. The following are equivalent: S(xs); nondegeneracy of every local intersection form on E_y; perfection of every degree-zero composition pairing Hom^0(B_y,M)×Hom^0(M,B_y)→End^0(B_y)=R; and equality of the actual multiplicity a_y of B_y in M with μ_y for every y<xs. The unconditional top summand is B_xs with multiplicity one, and under S(<xs) all remaining summands are unshifted B_y, as supplied by the comparison/classification lemma. No positivity of KL polynomials or conjecture at xs is assumed.
items.strategy: Use the comparison/classification lemma to write M=B_xs⊕⊕B_y^{a_y} with no shifts. Under S(<xs), the Hom formula computes the graded rank of Hom^bullet(B_y,M) as (H_y,H_xH_s). All powers in that polynomial are nonnegative and its constant term is μ_y because (H_y,H_z) has constant term δ_yz for KL basis elements. Polynomial scalars have nonnegative degree, so the dimension of the degree-zero Hom space is precisely that constant term. For the composition pairing, a composite between B_y and a different indecomposable summand cannot be a nonzero scalar: otherwise rescaling gives a retraction and forces that indecomposable to be B_y. Thus only the a_y identical summands contribute. Their scalar-coordinate pairing is the usual evaluation pairing of rank a_y; the adjoint identification with E_y preserves this rank even if the chosen splitting is not orthogonal. Therefore the local intersection form is nondegenerate exactly when a_y=dim E_y=μ_y. Character additivity gives ch(B_xs)=H_xs+Σ(μ_y-a_y)H_y. Independence of the KL basis proves that these multiplicity equalities are equivalent to S(xs). This supplies both directions of Soergel's omnibus lemma locally.

items.title: Embedding theorem: local intersection forms are isometric to primitive Lefschetz forms
items.statement: Fix x, s with xs > x and assume S(y) and HR(y) for all y < xs; fix embeddings and the induced forms, a reduced expression x of x and a generator c_bot of the one-dimensional space B_y^{-\ell(y)}. Then (1) the evaluation map iota: Hom(B_y,B_xB_s) -> (B_xB_s)^{-\ell(y)}, f -> f(c_bot), is injective with image contained in the primitive subspace P^{-\ell(y)}_rho = ker(rho^{\ell(y)+1}); (2) iota is an isometry up to the positive factor N = <rho^{\ell(y)}c_bot, c_bot>_{B_y} > 0: N (f,g)^{x,s}_y = (iota(f),iota(g))^{-\ell(y)}_rho for all f,g, where the right hand form is the Lefschetz form of B_xB_s with respect to the embedding into BS(xs); (3) consequently HR(x,s) implies S(xs) (Corollary 4.3: a definite form restricted to a subspace stays non-degenerate, so the local forms are non-degenerate and the detection theorem applies). The positivity of N uses HR(y) and the normalization <rho^{\ell(y)}c_bot,c_bot> = N > 0.
items.strategy: Write M=B_xB_s, ell=ell(y), and use the exact Delta-flag sequence 0→Delta_y=Gamma_{≥y}B_y→B_y→Q→0. Under S(y), ch(Q)=underline H_y-H_y lies in vZ_{≥0}[v] on the standard basis, because it consists of the actual lower support layers of B_y. Also ch(M)=underline H_x underline H_s has nonnegative standard coefficients from its actual support flag. The Hom formula and graded freeness give an exact sequence 0→Hom^bullet(Q,M)→Hom^bullet(B_y,M)→Hom^bullet(Delta_y,M)→0: left exactness identifies the kernel, and the graded Hom formula gives additive graded ranks for all three free modules. Their graded Hilbert series are those ranks times the same polynomial-ring Hilbert series. Hence the image has exactly the Hilbert series of the target in every degree, proving surjectivity (a mere ungraded rank comparison would not suffice). In degrees ≤0 the first module vanishes; hence degree-zero restriction is an isomorphism Hom^0(B_y,M)→Hom^0(Delta_y,M), while no full graded isomorphism is asserted. Hom(Delta_y,M) identifies with Gamma_yM shifted by ell, and the same degree bound makes Gamma_yM supported in degrees ≥ell. The support-layer inclusion is a right-module summand by the finite support-filtration/localization supplier; thus reduction injects its degree-ell part into Mbar^ell (if a vector belongs to Gamma_yM∩M R_+, project to that summand to put it in Gamma_yM R_+, whose degree-ell part is zero). A generator c of Delta_y maps to a nonzero generator of B_ybar^ell; evaluation at c therefore injects degree-zero Hom into Mbar^ell. Since HR(y) gives hL(y), rho^ell c_bot is a nonzero scalar multiple of c after reduction. If f(c_bot) vanished then f(rho^ell c_bot) would vanish, contradicting that injection. This proves injectivity of bottom evaluation. The reduced B_y is supported in [-ell,ell], so rho^{ell+1} annihilates c_bot after reduction, and bimodule linearity puts the image in P^{-ell}. For the isometry, g* f is the local scalar, so N(f,g)=<g* f(c_bot),rho^ell c_bot>_{B_y}=<f(c_bot),rho^ell g(c_bot)>_M, with N>0 by the normalized HR(y) form. Definite primitive forms restrict to definite forms on these images; the detection theorem then gives S(xs).

items.title: Hodge-Riemann relations hold for large positive deformation, and the deformation principle
items.statement: Let B be a Soergel bimodule satisfying hL and HR with the standard sign. Then for zeta >> 0 the induced operator L_zeta on BB_s satisfies hL and HR with the standard sign (Theorem 5.1). The proof contains the following signature comparison (Lemma 5.2): if V, W are finite dimensional graded spaces with graded non-degenerate forms and Lefschetz operators satisfying hL, W is even or odd, dim V = (v+v^{-1}) dim W, and W satisfies HR with the standard sign, then V satisfies HR with the standard sign if and only if for all i >= 0 the signature of the Lefschetz form on the primitive subspace P_W^{-i+1} equals the signature of the Lefschetz form on all of V^{-i}. Consequently (Corollary 5.3): if HR(x) holds and hL(x,s)_zeta holds for every zeta >= 0, then HR(x,s)_zeta holds for every zeta >= 0; and more generally the deformation principle: if hL(x,s)_zeta holds for all zeta >= 0 and HR(x,s)_zeta holds for a single zeta_0 >= 0, then HR(x,s)_zeta holds for all zeta >= 0 (signature constancy). In the signature comparison use the convention P_W^1=0; no positive-degree primitive space is introduced.
items.strategy: For the proof of Theorem 5.1 use the maps alpha(b) = b c_id and beta(b) = b c_s from Section 3.6: the forms in the images of beta vanish (since a positive-degree invariant alpha_s appears on the right), L_zeta agrees with L_0 on the image of beta, and the pairing between alpha and beta reduces to the Lefschetz form on B in one degree higher. Choose bases e_i of B^{-i-1} and p_j of the primitive subspace P^{-i+1}, note that rho e_i, p_j span B^{-i+1}, and compute the Gram matrix of the form on (BB_s)^{-i} with respect to alpha(rho e_i), beta(e_i), alpha(p_j): its determinant depends only on an invertible diagonal block J and on the block Q_zeta, whose limit lim_{zeta->infty} Q_zeta/zeta is the positive multiple i rho(alpha_s^\vee) Q of the matrix of the definite form on P^{-i+1}; hence Q_zeta is (definite) non-degenerate for zeta >> 0 with the same signature, the Gram matrix is non-degenerate, and L_zeta satisfies hL; Lemma 5.2 then transfers the HR signs. Corollary 5.3 combines Theorem 5.1 with the signature-constancy lemma. No choice is used beyond finite-dimensional linear algebra.

items.title: Minimal positive Rouquier complexes carry the induced Hodge-Riemann signs
items.statement: Assume S(<=x) and HR(y,s) for all y < x and simple s with ys > y. Fix a reduced expression x of x. Then F_x satisfies the Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations: there exists an embedding F_x \subseteq F_{s_1}...F_{s_m} such that for every tuple lambda = (lambda_{x'}) of strictly positive real numbers, each jF_x(-j) embedded in \bigoplus_{x' in pi(x,j)} BS(x') carries HR with respect to the rescaled form <,>_lambda and the Lefschetz operator given by left multiplication by rho, with the global sign fixed so that the Lefschetz form is positive definite on primitive subspaces in degrees congruent to -m+j modulo 4. Here pi(x,j) is the set of subexpressions of x obtained by deleting j letters and jF_x(-j) \subseteq \bigoplus_{x' in pi(x,j)}BS(x') is the canonical summand inclusion coming from F_x \subseteq F_{s_1}...F_{s_m}.
items.strategy: Induct on the Bruhat order as in the proof of Proposition 6.13. Write x = ys and use the last letter s. The inductive hypothesis gives an embedding of F_y with the HR property for every tuple of positive scalars; the complex F_x is a summand of F_yF_s, so jF_x(-j) is a summand of jF_yB_s(-j) \oplus j-1F_y(-j+1). Decompose jF_y(-j) = B_up \oplus B_down according to whether zs > z or zs < z. Under S, the canonical decomposition into isotypic components V_z \otimes B_z is available; B_upB_s is perverse and B_downB_s = B_down(1) \oplus B_down(-1); the change of decomposition is not orthogonal but the restriction of the Lefschetz form to B_down(1) vanishes by the degenerate shifted Lemma 2.5, and the projection of jF_x(-j) to B_downB_s lands in B_down(1) by the perversity of F_x, so that projection contributes nothing to the form. The remaining map jF_x(-j) -> B_upB_s \oplus j-1F_y(-j+1) is an isometry, and it is injective because applying the quotient functor q gives a split inclusion (a map from perverse degree 0 to perverse degree -1 vanishes after q). The codomain satisfies HR with the required global signs: j-1F_y(-j+1) by induction, and B_upB_s by the tensoring lemma applied to each summand B_z with zs > z; then the target is an orthogonal sum of HR spaces with matching signs, and the source is a rho-stable summand with symmetric Betti numbers, so Lemma 2.2 gives HR for the source. Proposition 6.12 (the tensoring lemma) is applied exactly to the summands of B_up.

items.title: The minimal Rouquier differential supplies the injectivity input of the weak-Lefschetz substitute
items.statement: Let x be reduced and F_x a minimal positive Rouquier complex. As a complex of graded right polynomial modules F_x is homotopy equivalent to the right module R(-ell(x)) in cohomological degree zero. Consequently its right reduction has H^j(overline{F_x})=R(-ell(x)) for j=0 and zero otherwise; the surviving generator has internal degree ell(x). This does not assert that the bimodule cohomology is the untwisted unit. If xs>x and S(≤x), the first differential of F_xF_s has source B_xB_s and target ^1F_xB_s⊕B_x(1); F_xF_s need not itself be minimal. Its reduced first differential is injective in internal degrees ≤ell(x), since reduced degree-zero cohomology is supported only in internal degree ell(xs)=ell(x)+1. Injectivity remains true after splitting off contractible summands that have zero degree-zero source. The form compatibility and commutation with the deformed operators used in the hard-Lefschetz proof are additional inputs from the factorization and HR suppliers; for zeta=0 descent pieces require the kernel-of-d_3 argument of that theorem.
items.strategy: For F_s=[B_s→R(1)], split the surjection as graded right modules. Its kernel is generated by (alpha_s⊗1-1⊗alpha_s)/2 in internal degree +1 and is the graph bimodule R_s(-1); as a right module it is R(-1). Thus F_s retracts onto this kernel as a right-module complex. More generally the raw tensor product has bimodule cohomology R_x(-ell(x)): tensoring the rank-one graph kernels gives R_x and adds the shifts, while freeness on the needed sides makes the tensor product preserve the quasi-isomorphisms. To obtain a right-module homotopy equivalence, inductively tensor each split right-module retraction with the next B_s and R(1); these maps are right-linear and all terms are free, and R_x is right-free rank one. Removing contractible bimodule summands preserves that retraction. Right reduction preserves the right-module homotopy equivalence, so the reduced cohomology is one copy of R in internal degree ell(x). Apply this to the reduced expression xs and F_xF_s (homotopy equivalent to F_{xs}). There is no negative cohomological term, so the kernel of the first differential is exactly H^0, with no vector in internal degrees ≤ell(x). Canceling a contractible pair in cohomological degrees 1 and 2 leaves this injectivity intact. This injectivity is obtained before any HR argument. Then use the independent positive factorization identity and operator commutation, and the correctly graded HR target W with map into W(1), to invoke the weak-Lefschetz substitute. Do not claim HR for the unsplit zero-parameter descent target; use the theorem's d_3 separation.

items.title: Hard Lefschetz for the deformed operator on B_x B_s, in the three cases
items.statement: The hard Lefschetz theorem for L_zeta on B_xB_s holds in the following three cases. (1) zeta > 0 and xs < x: under S(x), if hL(x) holds then hL(x,s)_zeta holds. The hL(x)-only descent implication, with the same matrix and no assumed S(x), is retained as an after-induction consequence in the character theorem, where S(x) has already been proved. (2) zeta > 0 and xs > x: if S(<=x), HR(z,t) for all z < x and simple t with zt > z, HRbar(<x,s)_zeta and HR(x) hold, then hL(x,s)_zeta holds. (3) zeta = 0 and xs > x: if S(<=x), HR(z,t) for all z < x and t with zt > z, HR(x) and hL(z) for all z < xs hold, then hL(x,s) holds. In the remaining case zeta=0 and xs<x, centered hard Lefschetz fails: in the decomposition B_x(1)⊕B_x(-1), L_0 is diagonal, but the first summand's bottom vector lies in degree -ell(x)-1 and its (ell(x)+1)-st rho power is zero. The opposite total degree is nonzero by self-duality. The two copies individually have Lefschetz strings centered at -1 and +1, rather than at zero. In case (1) the explicit form of L_zeta on B_xB_s = B_x(1) \oplus B_x(-1) is the matrix [[rho.(-), 0],[zeta rho(alpha_s^\vee), rho.(-)]], which after rescaling describes the action of a nilpotent element e of sl_2 on B_x \otimes V_2, whence hL. In case (2), the weak-Lefschetz substitute uses the HR target W=(^1F_x)(-1)B_s⊕B_x with a degree-one map into W(1). In case (3), first cancel the contractible shifted-descent piece, then use hL on the remaining descent component and the weak-Lefschetz substitute on the kernel of that component; the entire descent target need not satisfy centered HR.
items.strategy: Case (1): apply the local simple-invariants descent lemma under S(x). It gives B_x=N⊗_{R^s}R and the explicit reduced matrix [[rho,0],[zeta rho(alpha_s^vee),rho]] on B_x(1)⊕B_x(-1). The local supplier proves hL by an explicit binomial power calculation on each primitive rho string tensored with the centered two-dimensional string; the middle matrices have determinant 1 and the extreme map is multiplication by the nonzero integer m+1. At zeta=0 the bottom class b∈B_xbar^{-ell(x)} has degree -ell(x)-1 in B_x(1)bar and rho^{ell(x)+1}b=0, giving failure of centered hL. Case (2): put x=s_1...s_m, gamma_i=(s_{i-1}...s_1 rho)(alpha_{s_i}^vee)>0 and gamma_{m+1}=(x^{-1}rho)(alpha_s^vee)+zeta rho(alpha_s^vee)>0. The deleted-word factorization and chosen minimal-complex embedding give <b,L_zeta b'>=<phi b,phi b'>_gamma for the first differential phi:F_xF_s^0=B_xB_s→(^1F_x)B_s⊕B_x(1). After reduction it commutes with L_zeta on the first target and rho on B_x(1); the extra right zeta rho term on the second target vanishes. Reduced cohomology makes phi injective in degrees ≤ell(x). With W=(^1F_x)(-1)B_s⊕B_x, the map lands in W(1). The unshifted (^1F_x)(-1) has the induced HR signs by the Rouquier supplier, and its lower indecomposable summands satisfy HR(y,s)_zeta; the tensoring lemma gives HR on its B_s product. HR(x) supplies the other orthogonal target component. Positive rescalings preserve signs, so the weak-Lefschetz substitute gives injectivity of every L_zeta^k, and self-duality gives equal source/target dimensions. Case (3): take the same positive gamma scalars with zeta=0 and split (^1F_x)(-1)=B_up⊕B_down orthogonally, with summands B_y satisfying respectively ys>y and ys<y. The descent supplier applies to lower y since S(y) is known. Cancel the contractible tau_{≤-2}(B_down B_s(1)) against the next differential by the perverse lower-bound supplier; the remaining first differential is d=(d_1,d_2,d_3):B_xB_s→B_x(1)⊕B_up B_s(1)⊕B_down and remains injective in degrees ≤ell(x). All components commute with left rho. For a nonzero b in degree -k, if d_3(b)≠0, the assumed hL on every lower B_y gives rho^k d_3(b)≠0 and hence rho^k b≠0. Otherwise put V=ker d_3 and W=B_x⊕B_up B_s. The map (d_1,d_2):V→W(1) is injective in negative degrees and form-compatible: the removed shifted-descent piece has identically zero Lefschetz forms by the degenerate-shift lemma, so <phi b,phi b'>=<b,rho b'> on V. HR on W follows from HR(x), HR(y,s) for the ascent summands and the tensoring lemma. The weak-Lefschetz substitute gives rho^k injective on V^{-k}. These two cases give hL on the whole source by dimension symmetry. No step assumes HR for the unseparated zero-parameter descent target, and no step invokes the unconditional singular-category descent theorem.

items.title: Simultaneous induction: Soergel's conjecture, hard Lefschetz and the Hodge-Riemann relations hold for all elements
items.statement: Let X \subseteq S_n be a finite Bruhat ideal (closed under passage to lower elements). Assume: (1) HR(z,t)_zeta holds for all zeta >= 0, all z < zt with zt in X and all simple t; (2) HR(z,t)_zeta holds for all zeta > 0, all zt < z with z in X and all simple t. Then for every x in X the three statements S(x), hL(x), HR(x) hold. Since (1) and (2) hold for the initial ideal X_0 = {w : \ell(w) <= 2} by direct inspection of the rank-one and rank-two cases, and since the induction step preserves them when passing from X to X \cup {x'} with x' minimal in the complement and x' = xs, x in X, the theorem gives: for every w in S_n, S(w) (Soergel's conjecture for w), hL(w) and HR(w) hold; and for every x,s with xs > x the strong forms HRbar(x,s)_zeta hold for all zeta >= 0. The induction step: given (1),(2) for X, pick x' = xs minimal outside X; the hard Lefschetz theorems of the previous item give hL(x,s)_zeta for all zeta >= 0; combined with HR(x) and the large-deformation theorem this gives HR(x,s)_zeta for all zeta >= 0 (the deformation principle); the local intersection forms are then definite by the embedding theorem, hence non-degenerate, and the detection theorem gives S(x'); after evaluating at zeta=0, the undeformed restriction lemma gives HR(x') and hL(x') from HRbar(x,s)_0 and hL(x,s)_0; finally (2) for X \cup {x'} follows from the hL(z') case zeta > 0 and the large-deformation theorem applied at x'.
items.strategy: Assemble the four implications proved in the previous items: (i) S(<xs) and S^\pm(<xs,x,s) imply S(xs) (detection + embedding theorem); (ii) S(<xs) and HR(x,s) imply S^\pm(<xs,x,s) (embedding theorem, definiteness of subspaces of definite forms); (iii) S(<=x) and HR(<=x, lower) imply hL(x,s)_zeta for all zeta >= 0 (the three-case hard Lefschetz theorem); (iv) HR(x) and hL(x,s)_zeta for all zeta imply HR(x,s)_zeta for all zeta (large-deformation theorem + signature constancy). The passage from HR(x,s) to HR(xs) is the restriction to a direct summand and Lemma 2.2; the passage from HR(x,s)_zeta for all zeta to S(xs) uses the embedding theorem and the detection theorem. Base of the induction: X_0 = {w : \ell(w) <= 2}: for ell(w) <= 1 the computation is the rank-one example, for ell(w) = 2 (both sides in type A_2 inside S_n, or the degenerate case where w is a product of two distant reflections) the character and the Hodge-Riemann signs are checked directly from the rank-two decompositions and the rank-one forms. The induction is finite (S_n is finite) and uses no choice. Every passage from the tensor product to its top B_xs summand uses zeta=0, following deformation back to zero, and invokes the undeformed restriction lemma; never restrict the positive middle-position operator without an invariant-summand proof. For descent pairs keep the parameter interval (0,∞): choose a sufficiently large positive starting parameter and apply signature constancy on a compact interval joining it to the requested positive parameter. For ascent pairs use [0,∞) after the separate zero-parameter proof. Thus the descent failure at zero has no effect on the simultaneous induction. The base cases are calculated within the A proof (the elementary rank-one and two-factor forms); the B examples are illustrations and not prerequisites.

items.title: Soergel's character conjecture for type A
items.statement: For every w in S_n the character of the indecomposable type-A Soergel bimodule B_w^R equals the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element: ch(B_w^R) = H_w (the underbar H_w of the type-A Hecke page). Equivalently, the class [B_w^R] in the split Grothendieck group corresponds to H_w under the Hecke algebra isomorphism, and the extension of scalars of the rational B_w categorifies the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis. Moreover the hard Lefschetz property hL(w) and the Hodge-Riemann relations HR(w) hold for every w, with the signs of Theorem 1.4; and the same identities hold for the rational category by the base-change comparison. This is the main theorem of the pair: it proves Soergel's conjecture for type A, replacing the citation recorded on the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis page by a local proof. Finally, for every right descent xs<x, the matrix of L_zeta on B_xB_s=B_x(1)⊕B_x(-1) is [[rho,0],[zeta rho(alpha_s^vee),rho]]. For zeta>0, hL(x) implies hL(x,s)_zeta without an additional character hypothesis, since S(x) is now established for all x; at zeta=0 centered hL fails. This retains the unconditional descent claim as a downstream consequence of the induction rather than an imported prerequisite.
items.strategy: Apply the simultaneous induction theorem with X = S_n: it gives S(w) for all w, i.e. ch(B_w^R) = H_w by the definition of S(w) in the dictionary of hypotheses. The identification of the character with the class in the split Grothendieck group is the multiplicativity and the Hecke isomorphism of the published type-A Soergel page; the comparison with the rational category is the base-change lemma. No positivity is assumed from the published Kazhdan-Lusztig basis item; only its existence and triangularity are used to name H_w. Only after the simultaneous induction gives S(w) for every w, apply the local simple-invariants descent lemma and the positive-descent case of the deformed hard-Lefschetz theorem to obtain the unrestricted descent consequence. Thus the induction itself uses the conditional descent lemma solely on already-established lower subjects, and the stronger consequence creates no logical cycle.

items.title: Positivity of Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials, mu-coefficients and structure constants
items.statement: Write H_w = \Sigma_{y<=w}h_{y,w}H_y for the expansion of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element in the standard basis and H_xH_y = \Sigma_z mu^z_{x,y}H_z for the product of two Kazhdan-Lusztig basis elements in the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis. Then: (1) h_{y,w} in Z_{>=0}[v] for all y <= w; equivalently the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials P_{y,w}(q) = v^{-(\ell(w)-\ell(y))}h_{y,w}(v) with q = v^{-2} have non-negative integer coefficients, and in particular the mu-coefficients mu(y,w) = [v]h_{y,w} are non-negative; (2) mu^z_{x,y} in Z_{>=0}[v^{\pm1}], the structure constants of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis are non-negative; more precisely mu^z_{x,y} is the character of the multiplicity space of B_z in the tensor product B_x^R \otimes B_y^R, and equals the graded multiplicity of the indecomposable B_z in the decomposition; (3) also the expansion of the product ch(B_x)ch(B_y) in the standard basis has non-negative coefficients (the Delta-multiplicities of B_xB_y). No sentence of the published Kazhdan-Lusztig basis item proving positivity by citation is used; this corollary is the local proof of the positivity clause, based on the character theorem.
items.strategy: (1) By the character theorem ch(B_w^R) = H_w and by definition of the character the coefficient of H_y in ch(B_w^R) is the polynomial \Sigma_d (B_w : Delta_y(d))v^d with all multiplicities in Z_{>=0}; comparing with the expansion of H_w in the standard basis gives h_{y,w} = \Sigma_d(B_w:Delta_y(d))v^d, hence non-negative, and the classical normalization gives the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials. (2) Since the class map sends [B_z^R] to H_z (character theorem), the equality [B_x^R][B_y^R] = [B_x^R \otimes_R B_y^R] in the split Grothendieck group and the decomposition of the tensor product into indecomposables give H_xH_y = \Sigma_z m_zH_z with m_z in Z_{>=0}[v^{\pm1}]; the multiplicativity of the character over R is part of the base-change comparison. (3) is the same computation read in the standard basis, using that the filtrations of the tensor product have non-negative multiplicities. All uses are finite and choice-free.

title: Soergel Intersection Forms and Hodge Theory — Examples

items.title: Hard Lefschetz fails for a non-dominant degree-two element: the rank-one case
items.statement: In the rank-one case n = 2 the element rho' := x_1 + x_2 is a degree-two element of S with rho'(alpha_s^\vee) = 0, so it is not strictly dominant. Its action on the reduced rank-one Soergel module is zero: rho' = e_1 = x_1+x_2 is s-invariant and positive-degree, and x_1+x_2 = 1 \cdot e_1 acts on the right basis element c_id bar as the right action by an element of S_+, hence rho'.c_id bar = 0; a fortiori rho' cannot map (B_s bar)^{-1} = R c_id bar isomorphically to (B_s bar)^{1}. Therefore for rho' the hard Lefschetz property fails (the map on the -1 degree is the zero map), even though rho' is a symmetric degree-two endomorphism of the reduced module; the same failure occurs for every degree-two element with rho'(alpha_s^\vee) = 0. Consequently the strict dominance hypothesis on rho cannot be dropped from the hard Lefschetz and Hodge-Riemann theorems, and the constant term of the deformation L_zeta (the zeta = 0 case) is genuinely the delicate one.
items.strategy: For n=2, rho'=x_1+x_2 is s-invariant and has rho'(alpha_s^vee)=0 in the coordinate root normalization. In B_s=S⊗_{S^s}S(1), its invariance gives rho'⊗1=1⊗rho' exactly by the balanced tensor relation. Left rho' thus equals right rho' on the whole bimodule and acts as zero after right reduction. Both degree -1 and +1 reduced spaces have dimension one, so the degree-one Lefschetz map is zero and fails hL. More generally any degree-two rho' with rho'(alpha_s^vee)=0 has equal coordinate coefficients and is a scalar multiple of this invariant; the same argument applies. The bottom Lefschetz form is identically zero as well.

items.title: The rank-one Soergel bimodule: trace form, reduced module and hard Lefschetz
items.statement: Take n = 2, so S_n = {e,s} and B_s = S \otimes_{S^s} S(1) with the right S-basis {c_id, c_s} of degrees -1 and +1 and the relations c_id c_id = c_id, c_id c_s = c_s, c_s c_s = c_s alpha_s. The trace is Tr(a c_id + b c_s) = b for a,b in S and the intersection form has the Gram matrix [[<c_id,c_id>, <c_id,c_s>],[<c_s,c_id>,<c_s,c_s>]] = [[0,1],[1,alpha_s]] in the basis (c_id,c_s); its determinant is -1, so the form is non-degenerate, and the induced form on the reduced module is non-degenerate too. The reduced module has the real basis (c_id bar, c_s bar) with degrees -1 and +1, so dim(B_s bar)^{-1} = dim(B_s bar)^{1} = 1, and for rho = (x_1-x_2)/2 = alpha_s/2 (which is strictly dominant: rho(alpha_s^\vee) = 1) one computes rho.c_id = c_s bar and rho.c_s bar = 0; hence rho: (B_s bar)^{-1} -> (B_s bar)^{1} is an isomorphism, hard Lefschetz holds, the primitive subspace in degree -1 is the whole (B_s bar)^{-1}, and the Lefschetz form (a,b) = <a, rho b> is positive on it: <c_id bar, c_s bar> = 1 > 0, matching the Hodge-Riemann sign (-1)^{(-\ell(s)+1)/2} = +1. Finally ch(B_s) = H_s + v = H_s (the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element of the simple reflection), which is Soergel's conjecture at s, and the rational version over Q gives the same numbers.
items.strategy: Compute in the right S-basis {c_id, c_s}: the products are the displayed ones (EW (3.4)-(3.6)); the trace picks the coefficient of c_top = c_s; hence the Gram matrix. For the reduced module use the identification B_s bar = B_s \otimes_S R: the right action kills c_id.delta = 1 \otimes delta (since delta has positive degree) while c_s maps to the class of delta \otimes 1 = (1/2)alpha_s \otimes 1, a non-zero right-basis element; hence rho.c_id bar = c_s bar by rho.c_id = c_id.s(rho) + partial_s(rho)c_s = -c_id.rho + c_s and rho.c_id = (1/2)alpha_s \otimes 1 = c_s - c_id.rho = c_s mod B_s.S_+. Hard Lefschetz and the sign check are then immediate from the one-dimensional graded pieces. The character statement is the special case w = s of the character theorem, whose v-degree count matches the two Delta-layers of B_s.

items.title: The coinvariant algebra of S_3 as the Soergel bimodule of the longest element
items.statement: Take n = 3 and let w_0 = s_1s_2s_1 be the longest element of S_3. Then B_{w_0} = S \otimes_{S^{S_3}} S(3), and its reduced module is the coinvariant algebra C = S/(S^{S_3}_+) with the external shift removed: C has the Poincare polynomial 1 + 2t^2 + 2t^4 + t^6, so dim C = 6 and in the centered grading dim(B_{w_0} bar)^{-3} = dim(B_{w_0} bar)^3 = 1 and dim(B_{w_0} bar)^{-1} = dim(B_{w_0} bar)^1 = 2. The standard-basis expansion of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element is H_{w_0} = H_{w_0} + v(H_{s_1s_2}+H_{s_2s_1}) + v^2(H_{s_1}+H_{s_2}) + v^3, obtained by solving the bar-invariance and triangularity conditions with coefficients in v^dZ[v^{-2}]; its coefficients are non-negative and its value at v = 1 sums to 6 = dim C, and it agrees with the rank-one and rank-two Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial data P_{e,w_0} = P_{s_i,w_0} = P_{w,w_0} = 1 for \ell(w) = 2. Hence ch(B_{w_0}) = H_{w_0}: Soergel's conjecture holds for the longest element of S_3, and the Delta-multiplicities of the coinvariant bimodule are the six coefficients just displayed, one for each element of S_3.
items.strategy: Identify B_{w_0} with S \otimes_{S^{S_3}} S(3): for a finite Weyl group the longest indecomposable Soergel bimodule is the tensor product over the invariants (use the published rank-two longest-bimodule supplier, not a single graph bimodule), and its reduction is the coinvariant algebra by the Chevalley-Shephard-Todd theorem; compute the Poincare polynomial by the classical invariant-theoretic count (1+t^2)(1+t^2+t^4). Compute the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element H_{w_0} by the elementary algorithm: solve for a bar-invariant element of the form H_{w_0} + \Sigma_{y<w_0}a_yH_y with a_y in vZ[v], using bar(H_{w_0}) computed from H_{w_0} = H_{s_1}H_{s_2}H_{s_1} and bar(H_s) = H_s + v - v^{-1}; the solution has a_{s_1s_2} = a_{s_2s_1} = v, a_{s_1} = a_{s_2} = v^2 and a_e = v^3. Then compare with the Delta-filtration of the coinvariant algebra: the six layer multiplicities are the coefficients of H_{w_0}, and the sums match the Hilbert function in the centered grading. Record explicitly that the two sides agree term by term and that no positivity of Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials is assumed (the coefficients are computed directly).
