items.title: The rank-two Bott-Samelson bimodule B_sB_t: character, decomposition and the braid relation
items.statement: Take n = 3 and the two simple reflections s = s_1, t = s_2. The rank-two Bott-Samelson bimodule B_sB_t has character ch(B_sB_t) = ch(B_s)ch(B_t) = (H_s+v)(H_t+v) = H_{st}+vH_s+vH_t+v^2 in the standard basis, so its Delta-multiplicities are 1 at H_{st}, 1 at H_s and at H_t with shift v, and 1 at the identity with shift v^2; in particular all multiplicities are non-negative and the reduced module has dim(B_sB_t bar) = 1+1+1+1 = 4. In S_3 the product st has length 2, and the indecomposable B_{st} has the same character H_{st} = H_{st}+vH_s+vH_t+v^2, so B_sB_t = B_{st} is already indecomposable; equivalently the only summand is the top one B_{st} and all multiplicities m_y for y < st vanish. Similarly B_sB_tB_s = B_{sts} \oplus B_s with characters H_{sts}+H_s, and the rank-two type-A braid relation holds; the example also verifies the rank-two values of the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials P_{e,st} = P_{s,st} = P_{t,st} = 1 used on the companion page.
items.strategy: Use the multiplicativity of the character (published type-A standard character) with the rank-one values ch(B_s) = H_s+v and ch(B_t) = H_t+v (the rank-one example). Expand the product in the standard basis using H_sH_t = H_{st} (reduced product) to get H_{st}+vH_s+vH_t+v^2. Compute the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element H_{st} on this page by bar-invariance and triangularity (as in the rank-one computation but one step higher: bar(H_{st}) = H_{st}+(v-v^{-1})(H_s+H_t)+v^2-2+v^{-2}) to get H_{st} = H_{st}+vH_s+vH_t+v^2, which coincides with the character; hence B_{st} is the unique indecomposable with this character and B_sB_t is indecomposable. The braid relation for B_sB_tB_s follows from the published rank-two decomposition theorem, and the multiplicities m_y for y < st are read off from the equality of the two characters: all vanish. Record that the reduction to rank two is essential here (the design requires the examples to stop at rank two and forbids their use in the general induction).

items.title: Hard Lefschetz and the Hodge-Riemann signs for the coinvariant algebra of S_3
items.statement: For n=3 identify the centered reduced longest-element module with C(3), where C=R[x_1,x_2,x_3]/(e_1,e_2,e_3) has dimensions 1,2,2,1 in degrees 0,2,4,6. Thus the centered degrees are -3,-1,1,3. For every strictly dominant rho, hL is rho^3:C(3)^{-3}→C(3)^3 and rho:C(3)^{-1}→C(3)^1, both isomorphisms. The primitive spaces used in HR are P^{-3}=C(3)^{-3}, dimension one, and P^{-1}=ker(rho^2:C(3)^{-1}→C(3)^3), dimension one. Their Lefschetz forms are respectively positive and negative definite. The primitive decomposition consists of one length-four rho string and one length-two string. For an explicit strictly dominant choice let x=x_1, y=x_2, x_3=-x-y, rho=x_1-x_3=2x+y and normalize Tr(x^2y)=1. Then C=R[x,y]/(x^2+xy+y^2,x^3), with basis 1; x,y; x^2,xy; x^2y. The rho map from degree 2 to degree 4 has matrix [[2,-1],[1,1]], rho^3=6x^2y, P^{-1}=R y, and Tr(y rho y)=-2. These computations verify hL and the primitive signs directly in rank two.
items.strategy: Eliminate e_1 by x_3=-x-y. The remaining relations are x^2+xy+y^2=0 and x^2y+xy^2=0, equivalently x^2+xy+y^2=0 and x^3=0. Reduction gives the six displayed basis elements; their dimensions agree with the invariant-ring count, proving independence. The trace normalization is the positive standard top trace (the divided difference ∂_{w_0}(x^2y)=1). Compute rho x=2x^2+xy and rho y=-x^2+xy, so the middle Lefschetz map has determinant 3. The relations imply xy^2=-x^2y and y^3=0, hence rho^3=6x^2y. Also rho^2x=3x^2y and rho^2y=0, so the primitive kernel in centered degree -1 is exactly R y; its Lefschetz value is Tr(y rho y)=-2. The bottom primitive Lefschetz value is Tr(rho^3)=6. All other vectors lie in the two primitive strings and are not new HR primitive spaces. To cover arbitrary strictly dominant rho=a x+b y after removing its invariant component, dominance means a>b>0. The middle determinant is a^2-ab+b^2>0, rho^3=3ab(a-b)x^2y>0, and for p=a(a-2b)x-b(2a-b)y one has rho^2p=0 and Tr(p rho p)=-3ab(a-b)(a^2-ab+b^2)<0. These formulas give the full dominant-chamber verification without relying on the example as an induction supplier.
